claims.claim: Reviewers report that the game suffers from severe lag, running in slow motion or at extremely low frame rates that make it unplayable.

citations.review_text: Game runs slow af (like playing in slo-mo) making it impossible to play. vTried every "solution" possible I found online but nothing worked for me. My PC meets system requieremts so I have no idea what could be the problem. Was so excited to give this game a try but, alas, gonna have to wait for that issue to hopefully get fixed.

I really, really want to give this game a fair try. However, the performance issues are impossible to ignore and it severely degrades the experience. The game is absolutely devouring CPU cycles but feels unpleasantly sluggish. This should've been fixed before v1.0 released.

To explain: Everything happens far too slowly on large screens, such as on the farm or in town, while they play out normally in small spaces like your farmhouse. As such, even taking care of a few crops feels tedious because the watering can animation takes several seconds to play out.

If the performance issues are fixed in a hotfix I'll try again and likely update this review. Otherwise, this might be one of the rare games I get a refund for.

Really hoping they fix this issue and I can come back and give this game a good review, but currently I can't recommend it. The game is so laggy and slow that it is unplayable. I've seen a lot of other people say the same thing so hoping its fixed soon so I can give the game an honest try, but after taking an hour almost just to get through the prolouge due to lag I couldn't play anything past that.

lag makes the game virtually unplayable :( upon looking at the content of the game it has great potential! i see many others have this issue. currently playing on new macbook neo (ive never had issues w fps rates and lags w any other games such as stardew w over 180 mods, leafy corner, etc.) using the apple intelligence chip (i use parallels for windows). i tried capping at 60fps while turning off vsync and it did not change the performance. really hope a fix is in the works as im really wanting to play the game, but moving at one frame per second is quite unfortunate. totally get the game just launched so theres bound to be bugs! just hoping something is in the works! super cute artwork and overall great concept! until this is fixed i do not recommend buying the game.

I was very excited to try out this game, unfortunately it runs so slowly that I am unable to play it or even get past the prologue cut scenes. I tried as many of the suggestions to get the game to run more smoothly that I could, but none of them worked for me. If the performance issues ever get fixed I would love to try this game out.

citations.review_text:
I have been so excited to try this game out. Genuinely couldn't wait for 1.0 (I've been burned by early access before) and was super excited when 1.0 released. Finally got a chance to sit down today. There's screen jittering/flickering whenever I walk anywhere, and it's impossible to ignore. In the small amount of time I pushed through it, I got an awful headache. I tried every fix I saw recommended online, even changed my monitor's refresh rate, but nothing stops it, and as it is anything more than 15 minutes has given me a headache. I'm hopeful this will be fixed, so I can enjoy this game that I've heard so many good things about. 

I hate to leave a negative review because it really does seem great. It's just that as of right now, for me, it's nearly unplayable. I'm not the only person who has this issue either, based on the steam forum and reddit. 

To anyone looking for an opinion: currently it's a roll of the dice if you have issues or not. If you're willing to deal with the potential issues, go ahead and give it a shot. It looks great, seems super fun, and if it wasn't giving me headaches I'm sure I'd be sinking my time into it.

While the aesthetic is extremely cute and charming, and the world seems enticing, I cannot recommend this as is:

- Just walking around the world makes the FPS incredibly unstable. 
- I also encountered cases where WASD stopped moving my character, but arrow keys still allowed movement. 
- Text boxes would stutter if skipping text.
- Pixel font was hard to read in certain instances.

cohorts.summary: Players praise the swimming mechanic, automated watering cans, and direct storage crafting, though some note frame drops and precise placement difficulties.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the game features a jumping mechanic and swimming, which distinguishes it from standard farming simulators.

citations.review_text:
Whoa. Seriously, whoa. I've been hunting for a game to replace that Rune Factory 4 sized hole in my heart, and I think this is the one. 

The sprite animations are gorgeous, and the town setting is lovely. I honestly just adore the character in each sprite - caught a person sweeping her porch, and her hips had a jaunty waggle animation! It made her look so cheery there, just cleaning up her home. I smile each time I run by her.

I'm only a season in, but I haven't seen a single repeated conversation. Just like RF4 was famous for, each character has quirks, charm and a dialogue table 8 lightyears long. There are even little group conversations, where you can eavesdrop on their inter-personal relationships. It's fantastic!

Imagine my face when I accidentally JUMPED IN THE LAKE. You can swim!! And jump! I'm sure I will regret this as dungeons/mines get more complicated (I kid, I kid, I'm looking forward to it).

The game also doesn't hold your hand too much. I happened to discover several herbs and plants that were sneakily hiding as decorations, and each one has felt like a little triumph as I rebuild the farm.

The crafting is smooth, allows you to build/cook/craft multiple items at once - and takes stuff from your storage chests, which is always a win! One VERY interesting addition is that it takes time to craft items. You'll sit down to make 5 copper ingots, and lose an actual "hour" in the game day. Looks like there are talents and skills to alleviate that as you go, but I love how that affects your decision making - do you craft in the morning, or squeeze it in at night?

Combat is a step up from previous games I've tried, and I've only done a little bit of it. Early on, you unlock shovel-knight-pogo-stick-of-death, and I cackled so hard. The enemies are responsive, and the distance feels very accurate, so you can really dodge and slash with full control --- unlike in some games, where you feel like you just spam the slashy slashy hacky hacky button …

This game is very similar to Stardew Valley in some ways, but different in others. It's really nice that you can use spells to recover stamina and HP, grow plants, and more. I like that you can swim and jump, I really like the NPCs, and the stories seem well crafted. The Sailor Moon-style graphics are very beautiful, with an old-school feel. The game's fantasy theme and colors are relaxing on the eyes. 
The only downside is the jealousy factor when you romance someone, which isn't there: I would have liked at least an in-game option for this.

This is THE new farming game of the generation. It's like Stardew Valley but literally every aspect is improved and expanded upon and is much smoother to play (no Stardew shade intended). You can jump and swim! And it's 1.0 now!

claims.claim: This cohort reports that players do not need to manually refill watering cans, providing a quality-of-life improvement over similar farming games.

citations.review_text:
This might be my favourite game of all time. 
-I love how everything makes you feel like you're progressing towards something with the skill levels and the essence you get that you can use to upgrade a talent tree
-The interactions are very cute and I like the characters!
-I like how you only have to hangout every Friday with the characters so its not cumbersome if the social part isnt what you wanna focus on.
-There's a lot more QoL in this rather than in Stardew imo. Like how u dont have to fill the watering can, and you can always rename animals and houses, and place houses somewhere else, and how you can change your look wherever. 
-Another QoL is that you can turn off any negative things you dont like, like when marrying a chara if you were dating multiple you can turn off the breakup letters and you can turn off the missed sleep penalty etc.
-One more important QoL is that there's a little popup warning if its time to go home and its like perfectly timed for you to make it home from the mines.
-I think the artstyle is very cute
-The progression speed of the game itself (like big events and upgrades and location unlocks are very well spaced out)
-There's probably more and I might edit this review with more positives.

The ONLY negative is that on the Steamdeck its IMPOSSIBLE to like place stuff down where you want them... its really hard..

This game looked at farming games, asked "What is really annoying about these?" And then did away with all of them. Small quality of life changes like never having to refill your watering can or the only fishing system I don't hate really make a difference.

Name a farming game I've probably played it. This tops absolutely everything for me. You can tell the team behind this know their stuff and the community as the game is full of so many little quality of life upgrades that would dampen my enjoyment in other games.

Just to name a handful:

1. Can't cut down crops accidentally when clearing weeds
2. Bugs dont run away
3. Fishing doesn't have a stupid mini game
4. Very story driven
5. Chatting to everyone doesn't feel a chore, the characters are very charming and genuinely feels like youre getting to know them
6. Crafting is a treat. So easy
7. Map isn't overly complicated
8. Walking speed is perfect
9. I dont need to have the items in my pockets to craft with them. The crafting station takes stuff out of your chests and takes it into account
10. Dont need to refill the watering can 
11. Walking in and out of spaces is immediate, no loading times 

The game is just FUN and the characters and art style are so charming it's an absolute treat. And at this price too? A steal.

I am so glad I waited for the full release so I could dive into it fully without having to wait for updates. A massive shining standout of a game in a genre that has recently quickly grown into a slop factory.

TLDR: March I'm spending half my paycheck on your chocolate, please love me

So I'm about three hours in and the best way I can describe this game is comfort food well made. While Fields of Mistria isn't doing anything revolutionary, it IS a lot of fun, with the charming art style, nostalgic soundtrack, and great quality of life features--like for example when at the crafting stations, you don't need to have the materials in your inventory to craft certain items. You only need to have them in some kind of storage box.

citations.review_text:
Whoa. Seriously, whoa. I've been hunting for a game to replace that Rune Factory 4 sized hole in my heart, and I think this is the one. 

The sprite animations are gorgeous, and the town setting is lovely. I honestly just adore the character in each sprite - caught a person sweeping her porch, and her hips had a jaunty waggle animation! It made her look so cheery there, just cleaning up her home. I smile each time I run by her.

I'm only a season in, but I haven't seen a single repeated conversation. Just like RF4 was famous for, each character has quirks, charm and a dialogue table 8 lightyears long. There are even little group conversations, where you can eavesdrop on their inter-personal relationships. It's fantastic!

Imagine my face when I accidentally JUMPED IN THE LAKE. You can swim!! And jump! I'm sure I will regret this as dungeons/mines get more complicated (I kid, I kid, I'm looking forward to it).

The game also doesn't hold your hand too much. I happened to discover several herbs and plants that were sneakily hiding as decorations, and each one has felt like a little triumph as I rebuild the farm.

The crafting is smooth, allows you to build/cook/craft multiple items at once - and takes stuff from your storage chests, which is always a win! One VERY interesting addition is that it takes time to craft items. You'll sit down to make 5 copper ingots, and lose an actual "hour" in the game day. Looks like there are talents and skills to alleviate that as you go, but I love how that affects your decision making - do you craft in the morning, or squeeze it in at night?

Combat is a step up from previous games I've tried, and I've only done a little bit of it. Early on, you unlock shovel-knight-pogo-stick-of-death, and I cackled so hard. The enemies are responsive, and the distance feels very accurate, so you can really dodge and slash with full control --- unlike in some games, where you feel like you just spam the slashy slashy hacky hacky button …

Fields of Mistria is a great example of taking a familiar genre and putting your own spin on it.

The presentation immediately grabbed me. The overworld has a classic SNES Zelda feel, while the character portraits and art look like they came straight out of an 80s or 90s anime. It hits the nostalgia button hard without feeling like it's simply copying one particular game.

The core farming/life-sim loop is solid, with more emphasis on time management than maximizing automation. You're constantly deciding what you want to accomplish each day rather than working toward automating everything until the game essentially plays itself.

There's also plenty to do away from the farm. Exploration is rewarding, movement feels good, and the game has a lot of quality-of-life features that I'd normally expect to need mods for. Crafting from storage, easily locating characters, accessible shops, jumping, and swimming all remove unnecessary friction without removing the actual gameplay.

The mines deserve special mention. Combat isn't overly complicated, but different monsters have their own attacks and behaviors, so you're encouraged to react to what you're fighting instead of just running up and swinging until something dies. The different mine environments and enemies help keep mining from becoming completely mindless.

Crafting also has more depth than I initially expected. Many crafts have a chance at special infusions or higher-tier results, giving you a reason to invest in crafting skills and sometimes make an item again even after you already own it. It's a nice little loot-roll element in a genre where crafting can otherwise become very predictable.

Overall, Fields of Mistria doesn't reinvent the farming/life-sim genre, but it doesn't need to. It combines familiar ideas with great nostalgic presentation, good exploration, enjoyable combat, interesting crafting, and a ton of smart quality-of-life improvements.

If you grew up with SNES-era RPGs, classic Zelda…

claims.claim: Reviewers report heavy frame rate drops and performance issues during normal gameplay despite having high-end PC specifications.

citations.review_text: This is my first time playing a game like this on my PC instead of my switch, which has helped me to really enjoy the experience. I enjoy the graphics, the story is fine so far, and the character design is some of the best. I dont know why, but my PC frame rate will drop heavy during the game for no reason, especially when I am just walking in game and not doing anything crazy. I have pretty decent specs and can run big games with no issues like baldur's gate or elden ring, so I dont get why this game doesnt run great on my PC. Doesnt ruin my experience overall though, just annoying.

Edit: There was an update today that said it addressed lag issues but the first day I loaded up with the update was in the rain and the performance is still not great. Caught a bug in town that first night and that somehow caused the game to get stuck going at about half speed until I went to sleep. Alternating between half speed and normal speed over and over while running around near the carpenter happens a lot too. I would like to recommend this game as I think it does plenty of things well enough for the genre but right now I can't. The reason i can't is because just before 1.0 they swapped engines (out of necessity due to the size of the game they say) but the performance since that engine change is absolutely abysmal. The game slows to a crawl frequently even with very good PC specs and them still launching 1.0 in this state really soured me on the dev and the game. From comments it might be an AMD processor issue since that's what I use. The issues were known about as soon as they launched the new engine 2-3 weeks before the full launch, which is incredibly late to make a switch like that. I would consider the game currently unplayable unless you can tolerate frequent drops to half speed or less on a game that looks like it's from the SNES era.

This would be an absolute recommend if the game was optimized better. Lots of lagging, screen-tearing, and other graphics issues for a game that doesn't seem that demanding. I have tried capping the rate to 60 both in game and in my native graphics card's settings, played around with Vsync, and tried a handful of other fixes and settings combinations with no luck.

Oddly enough, the game used to run a lot smoother - it seems like the recent patches have made this issue more egregious.

claims.claim: The game includes quality-of-life features such as crafting directly from storage chests, real-time villager tracking on the map, shops remaining open without attendants, and an in-game appearance editor.

citations.review_text:
I have played and loved several Harvest Moon games, Rune Factory 4 and Stardew Valley, and Fields of Mistria has easily become a new favorite in the genre. It is clearly inspired by and a tribute to those farming sim games, with delightful references scattered throughout. 

What sets Fields of Mistria apart is its myriad quality-of-life features (no need to refill your watering can, crafting stations pull from all your chests, can shop at any business at any time regardless of whether someone is at the register, jumping!) and exceptionally delightful character dialogue. I have never felt so attached to the characters in a farming sim before; the children in particular are surprisingly fun. The system to collect "essence" by doing any action and spending it on skill points is so intuitive and low pressure, it is perhaps the best way I've seen a skill tree implemented for any cozy-style game. 

As for the negatives: The game can be a bit laggy on occasion, especially when I play on my laptop but it happens even on my nice PC (NVIDIA GeForce RTX 2070 Super and 16GB of RAM), but I expect performance issues will be ironed out in future updates. Several bugs have been cleaned up within weeks of release. I also hope some of the characters will get new poses (Juniper, March and Celine seem to have a much wider range of expressions than anyone else), that the map will show you the names of the characters when you hover over their icons (it is difficult to tell who's who sometimes), and that a festival will be added to the winter season (which currently has none). But these are all things that are likely to be addressed by the devs, and the game is still very enjoyable and worthwhile as of version 1.0.3. 

I am also very excited to see there is a growing modding community, which I plan to dive into as soon as I have completed the main story. I am currently in Fall of Year 2 and [spoiler] have reached level 85 in the mines with a town rank of silver, all but 3 skills max…

With 1.0 releasing today I figure it’s about time I leave a review for this amazing game!

I loved it so much in early access that I forced myself to put it down to wait and get the full experience in 1.0 and I’m so excited it’s finally here. For fans of the farm/life sim genre, I would say this game offers a familiar and comforting experience with a shedload of heart poured into it.

The basic mechanics are as you’d expect, farming, livestock rearing, story progression through the mines, making friends with locals etc, but each has their own extra little something and everything is just done so well. You can breed rare colours in your animals and use magic to water your crops, and it’s fun to stumble into a group of villagers doing some bug collecting or packing up their stall when the market ends - it makes the world feel more alive. The villagers are diverse, they comment on the things you’re doing in the town, and they each have their own little storylines going on. They really feel way more interesting than villagers in other similar games who repeat the same dialogue all the time and don’t react to the world around them.

There is also a bunch of QOL stuff that you love to see like crafting from storage from anywhere, no item durability, the ability to buy from shops even when no one is attending them, and the ability to edit your appearance from the in game menu. A lot of thought has also been put into being able to dress up your character with a variety of different aesthetic options, and there are also plenty of options for decorating your farm. If planning and decorating a beautiful home is part of the fun for you, you will enjoy that aspect in Mistria.

The one thing I would say, which isn’t necessarily a bad thing but worth noting, is there is a distinct lack of conflict in this game. The villagers (with a couple of notable exceptions) all adore you, and each other. Wherever you go in town you can see them talking to each other fondly and getting along a…

claims.claim: Some rare items and creatures, such as the snowball beetle, have extremely low drop or spawn rates.

citations.review_text:
Snowball Beetle spawn rate so low it's in the NEGATIVES.

Early Access aside, this game is missing a bunch of features that have NOT been announced to be added in 1.0 or at a later date. So no, I'm not including things coming to 1.0 in my complaints cause that would be ridiculous. That said, let's continue with my problems so far.

- The biggest issue is that you cannot make multiple save files easily. You have to be EXTREMELY careful as saves are limited and old ones will be rewritten. There is no easy way to differentiate your saves at first glance either, unless you completely change your characters name I guess. This means if you want to marry multiple characters... good luck. You are screwed over and forced to walk a tightrope to make that work. And the more characters you want to date, the worse it will become and the higher your chance of accidentally deleting one of your "other" saves cause you didn't realize you hit the cap and boom your oldest one is gone.
- Now, if you are interested in this cause you enjoy completing collections like the museum DO NOT BUY THIS GAME. The drop rates for some items and creatures (SNOWBALL. Cute standard farming game. If there's something you don't like doing (like mining or ranching), you still have to do it if you want to get further in the story. Combat is a bit clunky and I often get stuck on corners when I go fishing.
It often feels like I don't have enough time in a day to do everything I want, but overall it's very enjoyable.
it's a great game but i don't really know what to do after beating floor 100 in the mines and i hate the enemies that only take 1 damage at a time

It's as though the positive aspects of Stardew and the Harvest Moon series have been put into one game. Fields of Mistria is clearly a love-letter to the genre, and you can tell in its beautiful storytelling and well thought-out game mechanics. 
Mistria stands out in its characters, and the way they interact with the world and each other. They do not revolve around the player character, and it makes for an incredibly refreshing change of pace. You can listen in on conversations they have with each other, and discover who has beef with one another and talk to the town gossip to get juicy details or background information. 
The combat is the one complaint I have; it is a little clunky and takes some getting used to, but the variety of moves you can learn with the skill points does make up for it.

NOTE:  You must befriend Eiland and Juniper for a quest!  So start grinding them from the beginning!

Really good game, possibly a bit better than Stardew Valley.  (1) The dungeon/mine has significantly different biomes as you explore it. (2) There are a ton of different dialogues (didn't start seeing any bland/repeats at all until first winter) and they are highly context dependent (time/location/world events).

Fields of Mistria is a fantastic game. As a huge Stardew Valley fan this was a fresh take on the farming sim genre while clearly taking inspiration from both Stardew and Harvest Moon.

I found the art direction incredibly charming, the character sprites are varied and beautifully designed. All characters having seasonal attire is a great touch. The design of the mines in Mistria are also a strength. The level designs, monsters and progression are well done. Fishing, ranching, artifact hunting and foraging are all well done. I have no big issues with any of the game in its 1.0 state. The sheer amount of farm and farmer customization is also a huge strength of Fields of Mistria.

For me the number one selling point is the cast of characters and how they interact with you and the world. This is where for me Fields of Mistria outdoes Stardew Valley. In Stardew most of the character interactions revolve around you the farmer. In Mistria all of the townsfolk have already established relationships, friends, rivals, family, etc. You are able to both engage in conversations with multiple npcs at once or listen in on conversations between npcs not involving you. It creates a very well fleshed out cast of realistic characters many of which are a joy to learn more about and build bonds with. All of this carries over to the marriage and having a child mechanics. It does not feel like your spouse has suddenly been lobotomized after being married and having a child. There is a ton of interaction between your spouse, child and yourself as well as other npcs. Overall I was incredibly impressed with the depth put into the townsfolk and relationships in Fields of Mistria. It makes you really want to become a part of their lives.

I have a few small gripes, and I want to caveat that this is FoM in 1.0 and Stardew (in comparison) has a good decade ahead of them but there a few things they could definitely work on.
Buying items being locked into an even increase time when buying a large …

This game takes everything you love about Stardew Valley and harvest moon and makes it girlypop & pastels and its AMAZING. 

you can JUMP, quests have no time limit, you can be polyamorous while you date, the mines are diverse and contain cool mechanics, the storage is universal, the animals can breed different colors, and there's magic. 

it truly feels like the devs of this game looked through peoples biggest complaints of other farming sims and and tried to address all those issues from the start and they've done an amazing job. the 1.0 just released at the time of writing this and i have not yet explored the 1.0 udpates but suffice to say the Early Access version made this my favorite farming sim of all time and i'm excited to see what the future holds for Mistria

I absolutely love this game! The characters are super sweet, the music is amazing, and the whole atmosphere is charming and adorable. There are tons of cute outfits and decorations to unlock, everything is very customizable, and the game is very forgiving and relaxing. It took everything I loved from Stardew Valley and added a new cast and story and some major quality of life improvements, plus magic spells, animal breeding, and a few extra skills, including carpentry and a more fleshed out cooking system. I have a couple minor issues (mainly the combat doesn't feel very smooth and doesn't really have any stakes, and player dialogue choices usually don't matter) but overall it's become one of my favorite and most-played games.

Fields of mistria has quickly become my favorite farm sim of all time, there is not much i can say that has not been said. if you like farm sims? play it. I truly love it. good character, good art, good story, and a steal at this price. I have been playing since the first public demo and adore it.


as for my more critical feelings- I share in the hopes for future balancing updates from the devs

  I feel like post 100%-ing the mines should unlock ways to make going through them faster like stairs or bombs and the number of enemies that spawn should be decreased. or maybe an item/spell to clear enemies from the floor?

Enemy spawn in the mines feels way too high for how small the space is and for how much ore you need for things navigation becomes a slog in the late game. Tiny space bullet hell, is what it becomes. with multiple of the same enemy rushing me and me spamming my sword, rather than engaging with the enemies fight mechanics. Combat in general i think could be improved upon quite a bit.

real in game example - 3 projectile tossing enemies across the room while i need to make a bridge with my watering can when i just want to get some gold ore? or having 3 flying books rush me at the same time while i also have a fire sprite trying to light me on fire AND a slime AND 2 rocks- you get the point, too much. and late game they do not even damage me more than 1 hp so they are more an annoyance that slows me down from my task than a fun mechanic.

I think that there should be a way to mass delete manual saves or just better save organization in general. it's really easy to get lost if you are a save scummer like myself


I love this game i REALLY REALLY LOVE IT, but some of its mechanics could and should be rebalanced/improved. and I have hopes that they will. have fun farming!

citations.review_text: Loveee this game. It's very addicting and the art style is great. The mining is not overly difficult, you can raise super cute animals, and also the fishing mechanic is great. I appreciate several of the accessibility options like being able to turn off rain, snow, screen shake, etc. However, there are many flashbangs or flashing light sequences in some of the storylines even with screen flash turned off. They are also do not have an epilepsy warning as far as I'm aware. Overall a great cozy game.

I just wrapped up what i consider my playthrough of 1.0 after 100 hours, 2 in-game years, having accomplished all my goals. What a beautiful gem of a game. It is absolutely my top favorite in the genre. There's so many nice features and decisions that make this a joy to play from start to end. I love the characters, the dialogue, the art, the mines, the character customization, and everything. I really love the options as well. I was able to reconfigure controls and play one-handed after an injury. Slowing down time slightly, having no penalties or decay made a big difference. It was a stress free experience and I absolutely consumed it. 10/10. Keep it up!

citations.review_text: Absolutely a great time, fun characters and fun story. Progression feels great and I love exploring the mines. That said, the museum artefacts grind is horrendous, wouldn't recommend going for all achievements unless you're ready for a heavy rng-reliant grind.

It's a good game. Farm sim with the aesthetics of 90's shoujo anime. 


Everyone is going to compare it to Stardew so let me just point out how it's a bit different:


- Has a bigger dialogue table. You can talk to people more than once a day and they will usually comment on museum donations, upcoming character birthdays, Friday Night at the Inn, etc. This is probably the biggest draw for this game after the pixel art.


- Mines and combat are necessary in Mistria. This is for both story progression and romance.


- As of 1.0 release, the game heavily relies on RNG mechanics. It's been adjusted already but it still gets a bit rough between filling the museum, finding end game quest items, and trying to get certain furniture pieces from Merri, Balor's Cart or the Wishing Well. Recipes that drop exclusively from the mines can be a pain too.


- You can turn off break ups and keep dating other people once you get married. Note that this is a "non-cannon" function, so your extra partners will just act as if you never got married. Otherwise they send you a break up letter.


- Greater cosmetic variety in base Mistria compared to base Stardew, though it heavily leans towards girly and pastel.


- There is no divorce and you can't get rid of your baby if you get tired of it. Children are not required for a marriage though so this is avoidable so long as you choose not to have one from the beginning.


- Large livestock animals with enough affinity can be used as a mount. Livestock also have cosmetics you can unlock.


 Overall, the game is actually very very easy (minus everything being tied to rng). It's very easy to earn money. It's very easy to level up affection for towns people and livestock. It's very easy to level up skills. You get a full restore spell that restores ALL of your stamina and HP, on top of also having food which restores various amounts of stamina/hp AND potions too. You have a spell that summons rain and a spell that grows your crops. Combat is very …

claims.claim: In-game days pass relatively quickly, which can make activities like diving the mines feel restrictive without adjusting day length settings.

citations.review_text:
Fields of Mistria is equal parts farming sim, life sim, and dungeon diver--and it excels at each of those parts. 

Solid farming mechanics, a colorful blend of pixel and anime art styles, in-depth social features with a varied cast of interesting characters, extensive customization for yourself and your farm, and plenty of quality-of-life features that greatly improve your gaming experience.  

My only real concern is the mining-slash-dungeon-diving part of the game. Each day passes pretty quickly in Fields of Mistria, which is normally not an issue while farming but can get pretty restrictive while diving the mines for loot and resources. 

There is, however, an option to increase the length of each day from normal, longer, to longest. This option can be immensely helpful if you find the normal days to be a tad bit too restrictive. 

PS
I love the little homages paid to a certain game that heavily inspired Tales of Mistria, from a certain memorable costume to digging up the 'artifacts' aka the tools used in that certain game.

I think in a lot of ways this 'cozy game' falls in line with a lot of the others. Animal Crossing style fishing & bug catching. Stardew Valley mines. Seeing these kinds of things can kind of put you off playing seemingly the same game again. However, where this game differs makes it really stand out.

Biggest thing is the characters. They start out a bit too friendly. Very few real people act like golden retrievers when you first meet them. However, as the game goes on and you have more moments with them, these moments feel very earned and precious. Never really cared about characters in the other games (most feel one note), so this was a big plus for me.

Pacing of days & money making is also a cool distinction. The days are short, so everything just has you running around a little quickly, which I like. The best way to make money is actually to combine everything that you've found and make products to sell, versus other games like this where there is clearly an optimal crop/animal/bug to make a fortune off of. This makes (almost) everything you do feel valuable, as it will help you make SOMETHING to make you rich. Consequence of this is you might hoard a lot, but I think the trade off is worth it.

If you like 'cozy games' and you want more, then this will definitely scratch that itch.

quickly became one of my favourite games to play. The characters are engaging and very charming, and the romanceables are written very well in my opinion. I would recommend this to anyone looking for a relaxing and beautifully-written game and fans of the farming sim/cosy genre, but I do hope that anyone who comes across this game gives it a fair shot. I found the grinding quite manageable, though fair warning the time in-game goes quite fast compared to the likes of Stardew. I don't usually write reviews, but I would like to thank the devs for creating such a wonderful game. :)

citations.review_text: Buy this game twice, it's that good. Incredible story writing and characters, seemingly endless to do and upgrade and I truly cannot get enough of this game, I come back daily just to speak to people and progress the story. I am truly so glad I waited to play this game until full release because the romance is above and beyond all of my expectations, I'm over 100+ hours in and I still have a lot to do, don't let that discourage you but excite you like it did me. The only bugs I have seemingly encountered are: when it comes to Stillwell's monster quests I have to fully exit the mines for my kills to count, a bit of an annoyance for someone like me who grinds a lot, but I believe it could be fixed in game, not sure if it has been mentioned. The only other bug I have encountered are when you open a chest, FPS drops or freezes until the contents of the chest are out, and once the items in the chest are in your inventory these FPS drops and freezes stop, I've only noticed it with a chest opening (of any color) and these two minor things do not feel game breaking, and feel fixable.

This game is an absolute GEM. CHARMING. BUY IT.

If you need another reason, you can pet the dog. And the cat.

* Sometimes I get physically stuck with no visible reason why. For example, there are blocking items or landscape features on two sides of me, but the other two sides are clear. I cannot move in any direction, and sometimes can't even jump out of it. One time it happened in the mines and I had to get hit many times by an enemy in order to be "knocked out" of whatever stuck position I was in, even though I didn't change location.

Honestly just not for me. I've played for over 100 hours, I wanted to give it a genuine shot. I love Stardew and heard that this was apparently just as good, but honestly, I don't agree. I find certain things with this game to be very clunky, item sorting, storage/chests/combat/cutscences that take an entire day away, etc. I love that you can customize your character and the game looks very pretty. The game does not run super smooth, I feel like everytime I play it I have some kind of issue, getting stuck on walls, lagging severely, items disappearing, (I have made reports regarding these events). The main flaw for me is that I feel like it fails at the main gameplay loop, of getting a quest, collecting a bunch of crap, handing that crap in. This is the exact same as Stardew, but honestly, I find it so tedious in FoM. I feel like the RNG is never on my side in this game, one day i'll see a thousand of this specific bug I need, but then the day I get a quest requesting it, I never see it again. I had had multiple legendary bugs constantly respawning in one day (doesn't feel very legendary when that happens). Also, I don't know if its because I'm spoiled for how well planned the chests are in Stardew, but... I hate the chest system in this game. I feel like I have a thousand chests, and no matter how hard I try to be organized it doesn't matter. In Stardew, I basically have 6 chests total for an entire save, 1 per season, 1 for gems, 1 for misc items. I easily have like 15 different chests in FoM and I haven't even finished the game. Aside from the actual glitchyness or certain things still not being accessible (even after the final big update) this game is fine. In my opinion, no where near as good or thoughtful as Stardew. I'd probably give it a 6/10. Maybe with future updates it will improve my rating idk. I wont recommend it in the state it is in now.

Why wasn't this change made in the beta, if that is the case, instead of what should be the official version 1? I'm not playing again until whatever is causing this is fixed...really sad and disappointed about this.
